title: Binary Tree Maximum Path Sum
description: Find the largest sum along any nonempty path between nodes in the tree.
note: Track complete paths separately from the single-branch gain returned to each parent.
notes: This solution assumes a nonempty input tree. Starting res from root.val ensures that an all-negative tree still returns a node value. The optional root signature is retained; its initial field access checks presence at runtime when needed.

outer res in the dfs header allows max! to update the enclosing accumulator, matching Python's nonlocal res in the helper body. It is a writable capture, not a call argument; dfs still takes only the node. Each recursive call has its own node, left, and right locals.
max(0, dfs(child)) discards a child path when its gain is negative. An absent child contributes zero, while every candidate complete path still includes the current node.

max!(res, node.val + left + right) considers a complete path joining both child branches through the node. The helper returns node.val + max(left, right), extending through only one child so its parent can attach without creating a branching path.
The Python reference keeps the same traversal and expression order. LeetCode supplies TreeNode; the record declaration shows its standalone Birdie form. The tree is not modified.
Under unit-cost integer operations, time is O(n) and recursion space is O(h), where h is tree height. Integer arithmetic remains exact; the cases include a path sum above floating-point precision.
